subject: Clarify processor/service-provider scope for telemetry & subprocessor list
messages:
From: Beth Carter <beth.carter@acmeedge.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Cc: AcmeEdge Legal <legal@acmeedge.com>
Date: 2026-02-18T10:15:00-05:00
Subject: Initial questions on telemetry classification and subprocessors

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Our legal team asked me to circle back with a couple of narrow points so we can close the DPA addendum review quickly: 

1) For the telemetry we discussed (hashed device IDs, request latency, error-level stack traces with no raw PII), would Redwood confirm it is willing to be treated as a service provider under CCPA/CPRA for that telemetry (i.e., limited-use, no sale)?
2) We need a current subprocessor roster and an explanation of which subprocessors may process telemetry-derived identifiers. Can you include whether any subprocessors are outside the U.S. and whether you have an onshore fallback?
3) Evidence request: basic SOC 2 summary and confirmation of TLS in transit for ingestion endpoints. A redacted SOC2 or summary is fine at this stage.

I attached a short redline we received from our compliance team (see: redline-notes.pdf) but the main ask is the two items above so our contracts team can prepare the addendum.

Can you route to the right person on your side? If you can send the subprocessor CSV and a short reply on the classification we can move to DocuSign.

Best,
Beth
Beth Carter
Senior Counsel, AcmeEdge Systems
Beth.Carter@acmeedge.com
+1 415-555-0198

Attachments: redline-notes.pdf
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
To: Beth Carter <beth.carter@acmeedge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-18T11:03:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Initial questions on telemetry classification and subprocessors

Hi Beth — thanks, and great to meet yesterday. Looping in Marissa (Privacy Lead) and Aditya (SE) to provide the detailed artifacts. Quick answers up-front:

- Classification: Redwood is prepared to accept "service provider / processor" treatment for the telemetry bucket you described (hashed IDs + operational metrics) with a limited-use commitment and contractual language that precludes sale. We typically handle this via our US privacy addendum + a telemetry exhibit that narrows retention and use.
- Subprocessors: attaching our current roster (subprocessor-list-20260218.csv). We operate a small set of infra subprocessors (cloud infra, observability vendor, logging storage). Two of those vendors have U.S. regions and one is global but we have an onshore fallback option we can commit to for AcmeEdge.
- Evidence: attaching a short SOC2 summary (redwood-soc2-summary.pdf) and our standard ingestion TLS statement. We can provide a SOC2 report under NDA if needed — Marissa, can you confirm the usual approach?

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa to confirm the onshore fallback commitment and whether the telemetry exhibit language below suffices.
- If yes, we prepare a limited-use DPA addendum (we have a working draft) and share via DocuSign.

I'll also upload the attachments to the HubSpot record.

Thanks —
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
grace@redwood.ai | +1 206-555-0112

Attachments: subprocessor-list-20260218.csv, redwood-soc2-summary.pdf

On Wed, Feb 18, 2026 at 10:15 AM Beth Carter <beth.carter@acmeedge.com> wrote:
> Hi Grace,
> 
> Thanks for the demo yesterday...
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Beth Carter <beth.carter@acmeedge.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-18T12:27:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Initial questions on telemetry classification and subprocessors

Beth / Grace — thanks for the context. A few clarifications and proposed contract language.

1) Telemetry classification: based on your description (hashed device IDs, aggregated latency/error traces with hashes only), we can accept Service Provider (CPRA "service provider" / CCPA "service provider") status for that dataset. We will include explicit limited-use language: "Redwood will process telemetry data solely to provide, improve, secure, and support the Services and will not retain, sell, or use such data for targeted advertising."

2) Subprocessor detail & onshore fallback: the attached CSV lists current subprocessors. The single non-U.S. subprocessor that could theoretically process derived identifiers is our metrics aggregation vendor; we are prepared to put an onshore fallback in place for AcmeEdge where feasible and will commit to a 30-day operational switchover SLA for onshore routing if requested as part of the contract. Note this fallback is conditional on reasonable cooperation (routing DNS changes + capacity planning).

3) Retention and minimization: propose to add an exhibit that caps telemetry retention for hashed identifiers to 90 days by default for AcmeEdge with options to shorten on request. We will not retain raw PII in any telemetry pipeline.

4) Evidence: we can provide a SOC 2 summary (attached) and confirm TLS 1.2+ in transit. For a full SOC 2 report we will need an NDA and a time-limited sharing window — standard practice.

Proposed action items:
- Grace: share the draft DocuSign link once the contract team adds the limited-use paragraph + onshore fallback SLA and retention exhibit.
- Beth: confirm whether AcmeEdge needs the full SOC2 report or the summary. If full report, please route the NDA.

I pasted a short example clause below you can propose in edits: 
"Redwood will act as a service provider with respect to Telemetry Data (defined as aggregated usage metrics, hashed or pseudonymized device identifiers, and anonymized error traces). Redwood's use of Telemetry Data will be limited to providing, maintaining, and improving the Services and will not include sale, targeted advertising, or combining Telemetry Data with AcmeEdge customer PII for profiling."

Happy to hop on a 20-minute call if that helps.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Privacy Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0133

Subject: Re: Initial questions on telemetry classification and subprocessors

Marissa — this is helpful, thank you. A few follow ups: 

- The retention exhibit (90 days default) looks acceptable; can you add a short clause that allows AcmeEdge to request encrypted-at-rest retention for any exported logs?
- We will take the SOC 2 summary for now. Our InfoSec may ask for the full SOC2 later; we'll provide an NDA if/when that happens.
- Please add the proposed 30-day onshore fallback SLA into the addendum and confirm whether there is any expected cost associated with enabling the fallback (we'd like that to be included in the commercial schedule if there is).

If you can add those three items and send the updated addendum via DocuSign, we'll aim to sign within 3 business days. Thank you for the quick turnaround.

Best,
Beth
